observations.text:
Member verification integrated. No corrections needed — the member confirmed every check against real runs and edited nothing (`stop_confirmation.confirmed: true`, no unmanaged leftovers).

**Integration decision per finding**

| Finding | Decision |
|---|---|
| No missed requirements; function/CLI/USAGE.md all match | No change. Matches my own smoke test independently (bytes `Hello, Ada!\n`; stderr-only errors; 0/1/2). |
| Arity guard is additive beyond "accepts one name" | Keep. It is the smallest way to honor "accepts one name" without an unhandled traceback on 0/≥2 args, is documented in `USAGE.md`, and removes a crash path rather than adding a feature. |
| `greet(None)` → `AttributeError` | Keep, not a requirement gap: `requirements.md` specifies string names and blank-string `ValueError`. Adding a type check would widen scope with no cited requirement (`minimal-implementation`: delete-it-who-breaks). Recorded as known unspecified-input behavior. |
| `__pycache__/` artifact | Run artifact, not source; untouched. |

**Final state** — `greet.py` (30 lines): `greet(name)` strips → `Hello, <name>!`, `ValueError("name must not be blank")` when blank; CLI one arg → print greeting (exit 0), blank → stderr error (exit 1), wrong arity → stderr usage (exit 2). `USAGE.md`: command form, trimming example, blank-name error explanation with exit status, arity block. No tests, configs, or dependencies added — nothing in the requirement needs a permanent test.

Orbit task `c95c3f1d` remains active for the final independent check of this frozen version; any correction it raises wakes this session.
